title: Reported speech: what Díaz and Madero said

sections.content: You know reported speech with *dijo que* from B1 Unit 13. After a verb in the past, the verb inside moves back: the present becomes the *imperfecto* (*estoy preparado* becomes *dijo que estaba preparado*), the preterite becomes the *pluscuamperfecto* (*hubo un fraude* becomes *dijo que había habido un fraude*) and the future becomes the conditional (*aceptaré* becomes *dijo que aceptaría*). Use them to report what people said in 1908 and 1910.

items.spanish: En 1908, Díaz le dijo a un periodista que México estaba preparado para la democracia.
items.english: In 1908 Díaz told a journalist that Mexico was ready for democracy.

items.spanish: Díaz dijo que aceptaría un partido de oposición.
items.english: Díaz said that he would accept an opposition party.

items.spanish: El plan decía que las elecciones habían sido un fraude.
items.english: The plan said that the elections had been a fraud.

items.spanish: Madero decía que había que respetar la ley.
items.english: Madero said that the law had to be respected.

sections.content: Say who spoke, then *que*, then the verb in its shifted tense. Keep the sentence as a statement: *dijo que estaba*, not *dijo que estoy*. Retell what was said in your own words, without quotation marks.
